text:
Oliver: Proposal idea: implement a 'staged drain' state for prefixes instead of immediate eviction. Drain = keep resident data but stop any new prefetch/admit. Allow bounded inflight reads to finish.
Tia: How is that different from 'soft-demote'? sounds similar but i'd like clearer handoff semantics.
Oliver: Key diff: introduce a transferable 'drain token' that carries allowed inflight slots + expiry. Token can be read by new owner on takeover to decide if it must complete vs continue draining.
Hannah: Token shape suggestion: {epoch, allowed_inflight:int, expires_at:ts, persistent:bool}. Persist epoch+expires in lease store so takeover sees it.
Omar: Persisting on every demote event adds metadata writes. Are we sure we need durable token vs owner-local?
Bryce: For safety, takeover path is the tricky one. If owner crashes mid-drain and token was only local, new owner might evict prematurely -> RA-write violation. Persistent token avoids ambiguity.
Oliver: Agreed. But we can do a hybrid: owner-local by default, with a flag to persist for drains that exceed X seconds or when inflight>Y. That reduces metadata churn for quick churns.
Tia: What about memory accounting? Holding prefixes during drain could blow slab budgets under spikes. Need caps.
Hannah: Add drain admission controls: global_drain_bytes and per-tenant_drain_bytes. If admit would exceed caps, drain fails to immediate handoff.
Omar: Could we allow drain to 'spill' to disk (compress/evict-keys-without-values) as a backstop? That would keep metadata cheaply.
Bryce: Spill is complex but could be a pragmatic fallback: write a small tombstone blob so reads know to fetch from store rather than memory. Router negative cache helps.
Oliver: Flow sketch:
```
owner receives drain request -> allocate token (local or persisted) -> set state=DRAINING
reads that reference already-present KV allowed to continue (decrement token.allowed_inflight)
new prefetch/admit requests -> rejected with header X-Negative-Cache: drain, router caches negative for short ttl
periodic sweep: when allowed_inflight==0 OR now>expires_at -> complete drain -> evict/resign
```
Tia: Who returns negative cache? Owner or acceptor? Owner should return hint quickly so routers adapt. Also, routers should respect token epoch to avoid stale negative caches.
Hannah: Edge-case: a writer arrives at the same time as drain start. We must preserve write-after-read for that writer. Options: writer bumps a local pin/refcount (CAS) OR writer is forwarded to current owner while draining.
Omar: Forwarding keeps semantics simple: writer sees DRAINING and proxies its mutation to the draining owner for up to writer_forward_window (e.g., 2s). If forwarding fails, writer retries against new owner and may lose RA guarantee though.
Bryce: Alternatively, writer could CAS-increment allowed_inflight if the token still has capacity. But that requires atomic CAS against the persisted token which could be a small metadata hotspot.
Oliver: Tradeoffs: forwarding => extra RPCs but minimal metadata ops. CAS => consistent but more lease-store load. For canary we can start with forwarding.
Tia: Observability: emit events: drain.started{prefix,bytes,epoch,persisted}, drain.forwarded_writes, drain.completion{reason:expiry/zero-inflight/takeover}.
Hannah: Metrics: drain_hold_seconds histogram, drain_rejects per prefix, router_negative_cache_hits, write_forward_latency.
Omar: Rollout plan: implement owner-local staged drain + router negative hints + write-forwarding. Canary 3% traffic on single region for 72h. Manifested tests: simulate owner crash during active drain and verify new owner honors persisted token path later.
deploy-bot: Canary schedule: 03:15 UTC tomorrow, 3% hosts in us-west-2, revert window 6h. Auto-rollback triggers: >0.3% p99 increase, >0.1% RA-write error, or >5% increase in slab pressure.
Bryce: Playbook notes: if we see takeover-induced inconsistency, flip persisted token on and rerun canary. If slab pressure spikes, lower per-tenant cap and increase TTL for router negative cache to avoid repeated fetches.
Oliver: Implementation details: router maintains negative cache keyed by (prefix,drain_epoch) TTL 20s. Owner returns header 'X-NegCache:drain,epoch=E,expires=ts'.
Tia: Also add 'drain_epoch' to lease heartbeats so takeover sees a bump and can quickly reconcile.
Hannah: Add a small unit test harness: simulated cluster with owner crash, token persisted vs local, writer-forwarding latency and correctness asserts.
Omar: Nice. For long-term, we can evaluate a token-lease that lives in the lease store and is manipulated via atomic ops to enable safe CAS increments for writer pinning.
Bryce: OK agreed. Action items: Oliver will write RFC with state machine + metrics. Hannah will stub tests. Tia will add router negative cache changes. Omar will prototype write-forwarding. I'll wire deploy config.
Oliver: Thanks. If we keep the default non-persistent path conservative, we might get large benefits with minimal cost. I'll put the draft RFC up this afternoon.
